theme.title: Quiet Session
theme.summary: Technology (+0.24%) and Energy (+0.22%) led the market today, while Industrials (-0.48%) and Consumer Staples (-0.33%) brought up the rear. Performance didn't cluster cleanly by style — growth averaged -0.02%, defensives -0.17%, and value/cyclicals -0.01% — more a stock-by-stock market than a single broad theme. That shows up at the index level too: the blue-chip Dow gained -0.22% while the tech-heavy Nasdaq fell -1.33%, a wide enough gap to matter. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at -1.30%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX fell 1.01% to 15.68, which reads as an orderly rotation rather than panic-driven selling. Gold added 0.34% to $4,423.90, crude oil was little changed at $84.35, and bitcoin slipped 0.13% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
